messages:
pagerduty: :rotating_light: PagerDuty Alert — CardioEdge-prod reserved_pool_throttle fired (severity: P1)
incident-bot: page fired to eng-oncall, pager: devon (primary), maya (secondary)

devon: acked. I'm on it. What's the symptom? Latency vs 5xx?

ria: Customer reports elevated 500s and timeouts from their dashboard, started ~04:20 UTC. We've seen increased queued requests in the reserved pool.

oliver: metrics: reserved_pool/cardioedge-prod/util=98%, queue_len spikes to 420, avg latency 1.2s -> 3.8s and 5xx rate ~2.7%

devon: kvcache evictions spiking too? last week that caused similar tail latencies.

oliver: yes, kvcache_evictions/s = 1100, hit ratio dropped from 0.92 -> 0.65

devon: checking autoscaler logs, looks like scale-up failed due to quota error: "insufficient-gpu-quota" in node-group attach step

devon: /assign maya if I need help

maya: thanks. I'm coming in. esketching mitigation options: 1) route cardioedge traffic to fallback shared pool (lower perf but available) 2) bump reserved pool limit (need infra approval) 3) temporarily increase qps cap for their tenant to shed noncritical requests

devon: quick mitigation: start routing 10% -> fallback, verify error rate drop. I'll flip weight on router.

devon: command:
```
rwctl routing adjust --tenant cardioedge-prod --policy weighted --set "reserved:0.9,fallback-shared:0.1"
```

incident-bot: Routing change submitted by devon at 04:29 UTC — pending propagation

oliver: propagation done on 3/4 serving nodes. confirming metrics...

oliver: after shift: queue_len -> 210, latency 1.8s, 5xx -> 1.1%, kvcache evictions still high but stabilizing

ria: pinged CardioEdge account team and CS to let them know we're mitigating and will follow up. customer-facing note prepared.

devon: PagerDuty: escalated to infra team for quota removal, paging infra-oncall

pagerduty: PagerDuty: infra-oncall paged (reason: quota attach failure)

infra-oncall (susan): looking — quota hit is a regional cap from cloud provider. Can request soft limit increase; takes ~15-30m. Temporarily spinning new nodes in another region could work but requires routing change.

maya: for now let's keep weighted routing at 90/10. Need to monitor for a full-scale failover.

devon: Agreed. I'll also enable KV cache prewarm for cardioedge's hot prefixes to reduce eviction churn.

devon: command:
```
servectl prewarm --tenant cardioedge-prod --prefixes-file /tmp/cardio-hot-prefixes.txt
```

oliver: prewarm kicked off, logs show success for 18/20 prefixes

maya: status update for PD: mitigation in place, partial traffic shift to fallback, error rate down from 2.7% -> 1.1%. Residual impact minimal. Will continue monitoring for 30m. If autoscale quota cleared, we'll scale back.

devon: moving to handoff: I'm going offline in 25m, maya will take primary. tagging followup items:
- file incident ticket (INC-2915)
- postmortem with root cause: autoscaler failed due to quota, need proactive quota check for reserved pools
- run replay on prewarm coverage

maya: acknowledged. I'll pick up the postmortem and own customer comms. @ria please include the timeframe and mitigation steps in the customer note.

ria: will do. drafting now and will send to the account team for approval.

devon: final note before I hand off: set alert threshold lower for kvcache evictions and add a synthetic probe for reserved-pool attach failures.

maya: copying. Turning on a PD suppression rule for noisy low-severity alerts during this incident window.

pagerduty: Incident acked by devon, handed to maya at 05:02 UTC

incident-bot: followup ticket created: INC-2915 by maya — assigned to eng-runtime + infra

maya: closing loop here in ~30m with a resolution update. tagging meeting for postmortem tomorrow 09:00 UTC if root cause confirmed.

devon: :thumbsup:

ria: :white_check_mark: I'll update the customer thread with the mitigation summary and ETA for full resolution.

end-of-thread
